thread:
anya-support: Heads-up — customer (via Azure Marketplace) says their Marketplace invoice line items don't match what our dashboard shows for Feb. They see ~3.2M "compute units" on the Azure invoice but our usage shows ~1.1B tokens. They're escalating, asking for a reconciliation.
sam-billing: Can you drop the Azure invoice id + subscription id and a screenshot of the line items? Need the LineItemID(s) to correlate with our marketplace ingest.
anya-support: Invoice AZ-2026-02-789, subscription 0a1b2c. Screenshot uploaded to the case, and customer attached the marketplace CSV too (link in the ticket). They've highlighted two line items: SKU_A and SKU_B — totals 3,210,000 units.
maria-eng: Quick note — Azure Marketplace sometimes reports metered quantity in a different unit (e.g., "units" = 10k-token buckets) or in hours depending on the offer mapping. Also check timezone/partitioning windows (we ingest UTC, some partners report in local TZ).
sam-billing: Good call. For older offers we had a conversion: billable_units = ceil(tokens / 10000). That would shrink 1.1B tokens -> ~110k units, not 3.2M. So factor doesn't match exactly. Need to check if Azure is grouping per-request or per-model (embeddings vs completion) differently.
anya-support: Customer insists the invoice line items are only for the Redwood SKU. They said they didn't buy other SKUs. Asking why Azure's number is ~30x bigger than our billable_units.
elastic-billing-bot: [automated] Pulled marketplace settlement CSV for subscription 0a1b2c for 2026-02 and stored at https://s3.redwood-inference/private/marketplace/0a1b2c/AZ-2026-02-789.csv
maria-eng: I'm going to run a raw reconciliation against our ingestion. Steps I used locally:
1) Export our raw usage events for that subscription period:
```
SELECT event_id, model, tokens, timestamp
FROM redwood_billing.usage_events
WHERE marketplace_subscription = '0a1b2c'
  AND timestamp >= '2026-02-01' AND timestamp < '2026-03-01';
```
2) Sum tokens and compute billable_units = ceil(tokens/10000).
3) Cross-check distinct market_event_id to ensure dedupe worked.
Please don't share raw CSV with customer yet — we're validating.
sam-billing: I'll also check our offer mapping table `billing.offer_plan_mapping` to confirm which conversion rule applied to this partner. Sometimes a legacy mapping had meter="requests" which maps differently.
ops-sre: FYI there was a duplicate webhook bug we patched Jan 15 that could have led to duplicate metering events for marketplace partners who retried webhooks. Check `marketplace_event_id` dedupe logic in the ingester logs.
maria-eng: Preliminary numbers: SUM(tokens) = 1,100,234,567 -> billable_units = ceil(1,100,234,567/10000) = 110,024. That is far less than 3,210,000. Looking at the marketplace CSV we pulled (elastic-billing-bot link) I see multiple entries for the same meter with slightly different resource IDs — looks like they counted per-region or per-resource_id instead of deduping by marketplace_event_id.
sam-billing: If Azure's settlement flattening is counting each resource_id separately and we only emit a single marketplace_event_id per user request, that could explain multiplicative difference if the customer has multiple linked resources.
anya-support: I asked the customer to send the full line-item breakdown (they only sent the summary). Also asked them to confirm whether the subscription has multiple "listings" or linked registrations under the same subscription.
elastic-billing-bot: [automated] Ingest logs snippet for 0a1b2c: `2026-02-12T03:14:22Z marketplace_event_id=abcd1234 resource_id=redwood-001 status=ingested` ; `2026-02-12T03:14:22Z marketplace_event_id=abcd1234 resource_id=redwood-001 status=acknowledged`
sam-billing: Action items: 1) I'll open a ticket with Azure marketplace support referencing settlement id AZ-2026-02-789 and ask for LineItemID mapping + how they aggregate meter quantities; 2) ops-sre to confirm whether any duplicates were processed by our ingester in Feb; 3) maria-eng to run the final reconcile and produce a small reconciliation table (tokens -> our billable_units -> marketplace CSV units) to share with the customer.
ops-sre: I'll grep ingester logs and run a quick dedupe audit today: `kubectl logs -n billing deployment/billing-ingester | grep 0a1b2c | grep marketplace_event_id | wc -l` and check counts vs unique marketplace_event_id. If retries were double-processed, we should see more total rows than unique ids.
maria-eng: Once I have the reconcile, I'll post a short table in the ticket showing the mapping and any anomalies (duplicate resource_ids, timezone gaps). If it's our bug we'll credit the customer; if it's Azure settlement behavior we'll escalate with Azure and ask customer for a hold.
anya-support: Thanks team — I've told the customer we're investigating and expect an update in ~24 hours. @sam-billing let me know when you have the Azure ticket number and I'll link it to the customer's support case. :thumbsup:
sam-billing: Will do. Opening Azure ticket now, will paste case id when available.
